_: The words of every transition letter, one entry per situation. build-letters.py renders them. Twelve letters: five for situations (matured, lapsed, premium due, contract undelivered, application in progress); since 23 September 2026, five versions of the in-force letter by how long the client has held their longest policy (F1 under two years to F5 ten years or more), each asking for feedback first; and since 24 September 2026, two for clients in force whose cover ended and started again (R1 when the newest restart is inside three years, R2 before that), each offering a free check of the file and of who the policy pays. Every subject line is the notice itself, "{{agent_or_rep}} has moved on." and a short tail (24 September 2026: "on the subject line shall we put the names … more catchy"): the agent's first name where the sheet has it, "Your representative" where it does not. Facts are read off the Branch Portfolio sheet per client at send time; taps are the one-thumb answers, and tap_text relabels a tap for one letter without changing what it records; "questions" are the quick checks (one tap each, answered in the e-mail itself since 24 September 2026: "would like this as a check in the email! It must be easy for a client"), and "more" adds the one line to the full review for a client who wants to write. Beneath the facts, every letter carries the client's own record with the branch team (24 September 2026: "they are to see us as from onboarding and a team service"): documents handled, requests handled, premium reminders and the last birthday note, filled per client by service-record.py, a blank or zero cell cut like a blank fact; "service" lists the cells a letter shows, all four unless it says otherwise, and the premium and lapsed letters leave the reminders out. Days, dates and counts only, never a money figure. The notice that the representative has moved on is in the shell, once, on every letter; an opening never repeats it.

A.name: A policy has matured, or is about to
A.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. The money in your policy has not.
A.preheader: The money is yours. We want it to reach you on time, with what comes next talked through.
A.headline: Your policy has matured, or is about to.
A.open: It has reached the end of its term, or is about to, and the money is yours. We want it to reach you without delay, and we would like to sit with you and talk through what comes next.
A.notice_tail: The money in your policy has not.
A.send: Matured files first, then anything maturing within six months. The maturity date comes from policy admin, not the sheet; a blank date drops out of the strip. Most of this group is a phone call, and it is the one call nobody resents.

F1.name: In force — under two years
F1.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. Your policy has not.
F1.preheader: Nothing about your cover has changed. Tell us how the start has been.
F1.headline: You chose us recently. We are choosing you back.
F1.open: Your policy is still new, and nothing about it has changed: same cover, same premium, same beneficiaries. We would love to hear how the start has been for you, and what would make it better.
F1.send: In force, and the client's longest-held policy is under two years old. The newest relationships, with the least built up: the letter is about service and a named person, and asks how the start has been.

question_text.rating: How have we looked after you since you joined us?

F2.name: In force — two to three years
F2.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. Your policy has not.
F2.preheader: Same policy, same premium, same beneficiaries. Your view on the first years, in two minutes.
F2.headline: A couple of years in, and just getting started.
F2.open: Nothing about your cover has changed. Same policy, same premium, same beneficiaries. This is a good moment to check it still fits your life, so tell us what has changed for you and how we could look after you better.
F2.send: In force, longest-held policy two to three years old. Early enough that life has usually moved on since the policy was bought: the letter asks what has changed.

F3.name: In force — three to five years
F3.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. Your policy has not.
F3.preheader: Everything your policy has built is still yours. We would like your view.
F3.headline: A few years of cover, still yours.
F3.open: Everything your policy has built over the last few years is still yours, and nothing about it has changed. We would like to hear how those years have gone for you, and what you want from us next.
F3.send: In force, longest-held policy three to five years old. Value is building: the letter says it is still theirs and asks what they want next.

F4.name: In force — five to ten years
F4.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. Your policy has not.
F4.preheader: Same cover, same premium, same beneficiaries. Tell us how we have done.
F4.headline: Years of cover, and nothing lost.
F4.open: You have trusted us with your cover for years, and every one of them still counts. Nothing about your policy has changed. Tell us how we have done over that time, and what would make the years ahead better.
F4.send: In force, longest-held policy five to ten years old. Starting again elsewhere would cost these clients most of what they have built: the letter says every year still counts.

F5.name: In force — ten years or more
F5.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. Your policy has not.
F5.preheader: Every year of your cover is still yours. Your view matters most to us.
F5.headline: More than ten years together. Thank you.
F5.open: More than a decade of cover, and every year of it is still yours. Nothing about your policy has changed. You have been with us longer than most, so your view matters most: tell us how we have done.
F5.send: In force, longest-held policy ten years or more. Most of the fund value sits here: the letter thanks them first and asks for their view.

question_text.rating: After all these years, how have we looked after you?

R1.name: In force — cover started again in the last three years
R1.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. Your policy has not.
R1.preheader: A free check of what you hold today, what carried over, and who your policy pays.
R1.headline: A fresh start deserves a careful check.
R1.open: Our records show cover of yours that ended and started again in the last three years. A new policy starts some of its protections from day one, so we would like to check your file with you, free, and confirm who your policy pays.
R1.send: In force, and a policy of theirs lapsed or was surrendered within six months before, or a year after, another began, the newest such start inside the last three years. The new cover is still inside its first three years: the letter offers a free check of the file and of who the policy pays, and asks nothing about how it happened.

callme: A person sets out what you hold, what carried over and who it pays, then calls at a time you choose.

R2.name: In force — cover started again, more than three years ago
R2.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. Your policy has not.
R2.preheader: A free look at your file: what you hold, what carried over, and who your policy pays.
R2.headline: Years with us, and every one should count.
R2.open: You have been with Guardian Life for years, and our records show cover of yours that ended and started again along the way. We would like to go through your file together, free: what carried over, what started again, and who your policy pays.
R2.send: In force, with a policy that lapsed or was surrendered close to the start of another, more than three years ago. A long relationship with a break in it: the letter recognises the years, and offers the same free check of the file and of who the policy pays.

callme: A person sets out what you hold, what carried over and who it pays, then calls at a time you choose.

G.name: Lapsed
G.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. Your policy may still hold value.
G.preheader: A policy that stopped does not always stop being worth something.
G.headline: A policy you may have written off.
G.open: A policy that stopped being paid does not always stop mattering. Some still hold a value that belongs to you. Some can simply be started again. We would like to sit with you and find out which is true of yours.
G.notice_tail: Whatever your policy still holds is yours.

I.name: A premium showing as due
I.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. A premium is showing as due.
I.preheader: Already paid it? Tell us and we put the record right. Not yet? Nothing is lost.
I.headline: A premium is showing as due.
I.open: Nothing to worry about yet. It is usually one of three simple things: paid and not yet recorded, a change in how you pay, or it simply slipped past. Tap below and tell us which, and we take it from there.
I.act: Premiums or other payments due that are received by an agency, brokerage or a sales representative on behalf of an insurer shall be deemed to be received by the insurer notwithstanding any conditions or stipulations to the contrary.
I.plain: A premium you handed to a registered representative counts as paid to Guardian Life. Keep the receipt. And before anything can be forfeited, you must receive a written notice and twenty business days from it.
I.send: More than sixty on the Days column, after the paid-to date is checked against cash and the deduction file. Direct bill first. The days outstanding and the projected lapse date are printed from the sheet, so one letter serves every band; the receiving agent calls anyone over 180 days within two days.

J.name: Contract collected for delivery, never acknowledged
J.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. Has your policy contract reached you?
J.preheader: Your policy is in force. We need to be sure the contract itself reached you.
J.headline: Your policy is in force. Did your contract reach you?
J.open: Our record shows your policy contract was collected for delivery but never acknowledged as received. If it has not reached you, we bring it to you and go through every page together. If it has, one tap tells us, and nothing more is needed.
J.send: From Salesforce: the contract was received at the branch for delivery (the delivery-update e-mail, whose date is collected_on) and no acknowledgement followed; the undelivered-script chase confirms most of them. Goes in the first wave, and the receiving agent delivers within the week.

K.name: An application still in progress
K.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. Your application has not.
K.preheader: The cover you applied for starts when the policy is issued. Whatever is still needed, we bring to you.
K.headline: Let us finish your application, so your cover can start.
K.open: Until your policy is issued, the cover you applied for is not yet in place. So this one is ours to finish, not yours to chase: whatever is still needed, a medical, a document, a signature, we bring to you ourselves.
K.send: From the pending list: underwriting incomplete, missing requirements, awaiting settlement. Cover is not in place until the policy is issued, so these go in the first wave and an agent is assigned at once; every file is read before the call.

T.name: The agent's contract was terminated
T.subject: Your Guardian Life agent {{agent_name}} is no longer with Guardian Life.
T.preheader: Your policy is unaffected. Please read what has changed, and tell us if you have been contacted.
T.headline: An important notice about your agent.
T.open: From that date, nothing about your policy goes through {{agent_first_name}}: no premium, no form, no request. It all comes to our branch team, and we handle it for you directly. If {{agent_first_name}} has been in touch with you since {{terminated_on}}, please tell us below.
T.send: Every client on the book of an agent whose contract Guardian Life terminated, whatever they hold; the name and the date are read off the sheet (Agent, terminated_on). Goes before every other letter. The notice is in Guardian Life's own words and says nothing about why; Compliance reads it before the batch.

callme: Today or tomorrow, at a time you choose. We go through what you hold and who looks after it now.
paid: I have paid a premium that is not showing
Tell us when and how you paid, and keep the receipt. We check the record and confirm within two working days.
